EffectAddress.description: Canonical address of one admitted runtime effect.

ExecutionScope.description:
Stable semantic identity for one effectful runtime operation.

This is the scope admitted by the host boundary before nondeterministic
work begins. Its journal encoding is an existing durable contract; effect
addresses compose it with a replay key without changing those bytes.

oneOf.description:
One operation on a session that runs no turn: a host command, named
by its batch, or the admissions of one shift request. It has no
logical root, and no logical turn runs under it.

ExprSlot.description:
The role one child expression plays in its parent expression of the
shared workflow IR.

oneOf.description: A statement of a block or an element of a list.
The value of a record entry, by entry position.
The expression a label or a structural role wraps.
A dynamic index of an assignment target's path, by position.
The value an assignment stores.
The generated statements that bind a loop element to authored names.
The body of a loop, a function, a process literal or a `try`.
The input of a host descriptor constructor.
A call argument, by position.
The single operand of a unary form.
The computed member a method call reads its callee from.
The collection a map intrinsic reads.
The callback a map intrinsic applies.

ModuleRef.description: The content-addressed stored VM module an execution document names.

RunAggregateWakePolicy.description:
Aggregate wake rule. Run-owned aggregates preserve these semantics;
the rule does not require a durable group dispatcher.

`Promise.all` and `Promise.allSettled` both use [`All`](Self::All): the
caller's early exit on rejection is not a host wake rule. The wire shape
has no default, so a missing rule cannot be replayed under a guess.

oneOf.description: Wake on the first settlement of any kind.
Wake on the first success, or after every child fails.
Deliver every settlement in durable rank order.

StepBodyStarted.description:
The admitted body of a process step started: the step's actor committed
its admission, bound it to a call, and is about to run it. A step that is
refused never produces one, and a retried body produces one more with the
same site, occurrence and call and the next attempt.

It names no language and no document: the process's own definition scopes
the site.

at.description:
The occurrence of the site in the process's workflow document the
step runs for.

attempt.description: The one-based attempt of the admitted body.

call_id.description: The call the admission bound the step to.

TraceLanguageExecutionFailure.description: The observed cause of a failed language node.

oneOf.description:
A dispatched tool effect failed with its recorded classification and
recorded source and delay hint. `replay_key` is the causing effect's identity.
A VM or host-boundary failure with a stable runtime error code.

The execution began. Its identity names the workflow document and
entry; the document itself is read through facade workflow inspection.
One fact about one occurrence of one execution site.

TraceNodeFact.description:
What happened to the occurrence a
[`TraceLanguageExecutionPayload::Node`] names.

oneOf.description:
The occurrence has parked on an observed wait. Its `since` is the
enclosing trace record timestamp, not a separately sampled clock.

A parked occurrence resolved, including cancellation. Its node
terminal remains a separate fact.
Only an occurrence observed in flight may be cancelled.

selected.description: The arm of the branch this occurrence took.

oneOf.description: The occurrence started a child execution.
The module's main body.

One exported process, by the persisted reference the module's
exports name it with.

WorkflowDocumentRef.description:
Which workflow document an execution runs, and where it enters it. It
names the document; it is never the document. A host reads the graph the
reference names through the facade's workflow inspection and may cache
it under this value, which is immutable for a process.

entry.description: Where the execution enters the document.

ir_version.description: The interpretation of the IR the document is written under.

module_ref.description: The stored module the document is read from.

source_identity.description:
The definition identity of the admitted module the document
projects; the document's own `source_identity`.

WorkflowLoopFrame.description: One enclosing loop of an occurrence, outermost first in a context.

activation.description:
Which entry of that loop this is, unique within the execution: a loop
reentered by an outer iteration gets a new activation.

WorkflowLoopPosition.description: Where inside one loop activation something ran. Numbers are one-based.

oneOf.description:
The `n`-th evaluation of a `while` condition. The check after the last
body iteration, which reads false, is a check with no body of its
number.
The `n`-th run of the loop body.

WorkflowNodeId.description:
A deterministic node identifier of a workflow document, minted from the
node's structural owner and AST path. It is never empty.

WorkflowOccurrence.description:
One occurrence of one execution site: the site, which run of that site
this is (from 1, counted per site within an execution), and the loop
activations that enclosed the occurrence when it began, outermost first.

Every layer that names an occurrence (durable effect and wait records,
trace facts, the overlay and the VM) holds this value.

WorkflowOverlayCall.description: The admitted call an occurrence is bound to.

attempt.description:
The latest attempt of the call's admitted body that was observed to
start; absent when the binding came from a language fact alone.

WorkflowOverlayChildLink.description:
Link from an observed parent site to a child execution's overlay. The
parent execution is the overlay's own.

WorkflowOverlayConflict.description:
A bounded, typed record of divergent observations under one identity.
The overlay keeps the earlier observation; of two at one instant it keeps
the one whose variant digest is smaller. `variants` lists the smallest and
the largest digest observed.

WorkflowOverlayConflictKind.description: Why two records under one logical identity did not deduplicate.

WorkflowOverlayCoverage.description: How much of the execution the overlay can speak for.

start_observed.description:
The retained observations include the execution's start. Without it
the observer attached late or lost continuity, and occurrences that
ran before are not here.

WorkflowOverlayDocumentBinding.description: What the overlay knows of the document its execution runs.

oneOf.description: No document was given and the execution's start was not observed.

The execution's start named this document; the reducer was not given
it, so the listed sites are whatever was observed.

The reducer was given this document: every listed site is one of its
sites, and a site it lacks is a mismatch.

WorkflowOverlayEventIdentity.description:
Canonical identity of one observation within its execution: two
observations with one identity are of the same transition.

An execution starts once and finishes once. An occurrence starts, ends,
selects a branch and starts a child once each, and may wait and resume
any number of times: each wait and each resume is its own observation,
numbered in time. A step body start is one fact per attempt of its body.

WorkflowOverlayHistoryEvent.description:
One canonical observation retained so a persisted overlay can be folded
again.

oneOf.description: What the language execution reported.
The admitted body of a process step started.

WorkflowOverlayMismatch.description:
An observation that does not belong to the claimed document. It is
reported and never folded into the overlay.

oneOf.description: The execution's start names another document than the one loaded.
An observation names a site the loaded document does not have.
The occurrence's `ordinal`-th retained wait, from 1, in time order.
The occurrence's `ordinal`-th retained resume, from 1, in time order.
The occurrence completed, failed or was cancelled.

WorkflowOverlaySettlement.description:
Terminal evidence supplied by a committed process fact or durable snapshot.
This does not manufacture a language execution or site observation.

occurred_at.description: None when the snapshot has no canonical terminal occurrence time.

WorkflowOverlaySite.description: What was observed at one execution site of the document.

oneOf.description:
The process settled without complete terminal evidence for this
observed occurrence. The category is authoritative; success, failure
and timing are not inferred from it.

branch.description:
Which arm a branch site last took. Absent on every other site, and on
a branch whose selection has not been observed. The arms themselves
are the document's: a host reads which nodes an unselected arm holds
from the branch's typed children.

call.description: The admitted call of the site's latest bound occurrence.

WorkflowOverlaySiteRetention.description:
What one site keeps of the occurrences evicted from its bounded history.

Occurrences at or below `truncation_watermark` are no longer in the
overlay's history. The watermark occurrence keeps its observations, so
one that arrives late still folds exactly. The occurrences below it are
folded into `archived`; of those, a late observation can refine only the
occurrence `archived` shows.

archived.description: What the occurrences below the watermark folded to.

archived_children.description: The child executions the occurrences below the watermark started.

watermark_history.description: The observations of the watermark occurrence.

WorkflowOverlaySiteState.description: What a site's occurrences fold to.

oneOf.description:
The process settled without complete terminal evidence for this
observed occurrence. The category is authoritative; success, failure
and timing are not inferred from it.

branch.description:
Which arm a branch site last took. Absent on every other site, and on
a branch whose selection has not been observed. The arms themselves
are the document's: a host reads which nodes an unselected arm holds
from the branch's typed children.

call.description: The admitted call of the site's latest bound occurrence.

WorkflowOverlayTerminal.description: The actual durable terminal category; abandonment is not a VM failure.

WorkflowSitePath.description:
The address of one execution site inside a workflow node: the slot path
from the node's statement to the site's expression, and the synthetic
site of that expression it names, if it is not the expression's own. The
default is the statement's own site.

WorkflowSiteRef.description:
The static address of one execution site in a workflow document: the node
that owns it and the path to the executable subexpression inside it.

WorkflowSiteRole.description: What a site that is not an expression of its own stands for.

oneOf.description:
The step a label declares over the expression it wraps, when that
expression is not itself the labeled operation.

WorkflowSlotPath.description:
The typed path from a workflow node's statement to one expression inside
it: the child slot taken at each step. The empty path is the statement
itself.

The serialized list is authoritative. [`Display`](std::fmt::Display) is a
derived spelling for text-only host contracts.

description:
What one execution did, keyed into the workflow document it ran.

The overlay holds only what was observed: per-site occurrence states,
branch choices, child links and the bounded history they fold from. The
static structure (nodes, labels, kinds, edges, the arms of a branch) is
the document's; a site with no observation is not listed here.

mismatches.description:
Observations that did not belong to the document, smallest first, at
most 64.

mismatches_truncated.description: More mismatches were observed than `mismatches` lists.

settlement.description: Authoritative process settlement, independent of provisional VM outcomes.
